newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares, Western demand, stable.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares, Western demand, stable.

text.p: Leading Russian shares closed steady on Wednesday, propped up near record levels by unaggressive Western demand, traders said, forecasting a stable market on Thursday.

"The market is steady and tomorrow will be the same," said UCB securities director Dmitry Yevenko. "I would expect small price swings...but in general we are inclined towards growth, which we see closer to June."

The Russian Trading System 22-share index closed at 338.70, down from 339.04 on Tuesday and the record 349.27 set on February 20. Share prices dipped after that until about April 25. Volume was $28.1 million on Wednesday.
National power company UES EESR.RTS rose to $0.2775 from $0.2750, local power utility Mosenergo MSNG.RTS rose to $1.365 from $1.351 and oil producer LUKoil LKOH.RTS eased to $14.44 from $14.53.
Tatneft TATN.RTS oil company rose to $80.40 from $77.00 after the autonomous Tatar Republic, where Tatneft is based, adopted a new oil and gas law.
"No one is taking aggressive volumes, but all the same everyone is buying between the holidays," Yevenko said. Russian markets were closed last May 1-4 and will be closed on May 9-11.
Volume dropped below healthy market levels on Wednesday after three trading days above $40 million reported turnover, which is generally seen as a healthy volume.
Traders said Western demand was behind most buying.
But Vostochnya Investitsionnaya trader Konstantin Maslennikov said Russians were quietly taking profits while Westerners quietly bought.
